_comment: Applications ZUZZ may open without an extra prompt. The key is what the
user types; the value is what gets launched. An app that is NOT here can
still be opened, but it is mapped to run_safe_commands and so asks at every
trust level rather than auto-approving like the entries below.
This file is re-read on every lookup, so an edit takes effect without a restart.
The whitelist is a convenience, not a security boundary: it removes prompts, it
does not grant access. An application that is not here is still launchable, it
Removing an entry does not block that app, it only removes the auto-approval.
